formula: burg09 ~ act.comp + I(tuition / 1000) + I(total / 1000) + act.comp:I(tuition / 1000) + act.comp:I(total / 1000) + (1 | state)
notes: Second reading of a flat table. BeyondMLR (Roback and Legler 2021) ch. 4 guided exercise 5 (https://bookdown.org/roback/bookdown-BeyondMLR/ch-poissonreg.html) gives burg09, the burglaries reported in 2009 at a collection of U.S. public universities with over 10,000 students, and fits single-level models: lm on act.comp, tuition, pct.male and total (b), Poisson regressions on the same (c) and with tuition.thous = tuition/1000 (d), with log(total) as an offset or as a predictor (e), and last glm(..., family = poisson) on act.comp, tuition.thous and total.thous = total/1000 with the act.comp:tuition.thous and act.comp:total.thous interactions (f), filed here. The universities repeat within state, many states holding several and about half one, so the random intercept for state, an area factor sampled from the U.S. states as HSAUR3 Forbes2000's country, is the reader's proposal; no source fits it. sat.tot is the mean of sat.math and sat.read; pct.male is 100 * mentotal / total. Outside check: stands.

Its example fits fitme(cbind(pos1046738,1-pos1046738)~seasonal+Matern(1|LAT+LONG), family=binomial(), method='PQL/L', data=arabidopsis), 'The response is binary', first with rho, nu and lambda fixed at values 'deduced from the following fit', then estimated (Rousset and Ferdy 2014). LAT and LONG identify the collection sites, many holding several accessions with the same climatic values, and the Matern random effect takes one value per distinct location, so LAT:LONG is the grouping factor, as pymc_examples gambia_dataset's x:y; the first reading's coordinate rule covers coordinates each row holds once (besag.checks). pos5510910, pos6235221 and pos8132698 are the other SNPs, no model of the page; the other climatic variables are unused.
